report:
Reviewed the complete blessing_gate claim, all three ordinary implementation associations (CompileTest::run/prepare in mod.rs, observe::collect, and rustc::check), both complete associated test bodies, and captured annotation-parser and review/RFD context. There are no TODO or N/A entries.

Preparation ordering: run calls prepare and panics on Err before accessing any of its three expectation assertions. prepare validates paths/root/conflicts and edition, parses annotations and checks observation expectation presence, materializes the isolated fixture, invokes rustc independently, and opens the production Sage host. observe::collect checks the crate, validates marker membership, freezes the inspection log, performs Sage diagnostic matching, validates and renders requested type/symbol observations, projects and serializes requested query events, and renders diagnostics into owned strings. The final prepare match returns Output only if both Sage preparation and rustc validation succeeded. A rustc failure remains a failure even if Sage output was successfully rendered; Sage errors likewise cannot be bypassed by rustc success. Fixture, annotation, compiler execution, matching, observation, query projection, or rendering failures cannot reach expectation comparison. No helper receives expectation assertions, and preparation itself never calls expect-test. The boundary comment explicitly states why all validated rendered outputs must return first, fulfilling the structural explanation requirement without a filesystem transaction.

Exhaustiveness: both compiler paths call the shared compiler-aware matcher, which selects applicable diagnostic markers, constructs severity/location edges, finds a complete one-to-one assignment, and rejects either unmatched markers or unassigned diagnostics. rustc::check validates execution and parsed output before matching. Marker parsing constructs immutable conditions from source; neither compiler path or updating comparison rewrites markers or compiler qualifications. On successful preparation, run compares observations, diagnostics, and optional queries separately, enabling their representation updates. The contract covers one invocation's preparation barrier, not rollback of later expect-test I/O failures or other independent tests.

Test adequacy: blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates visibly creates a disposable callsite, introduces an unmatched rustc-only warning while an observation expectation is stale, runs UPDATE_EXPECT=1 expecting failure, requires the Rustc matching error, and checks the entire file is byte-for-byte unchanged. It then checks a stale expectation fails without updating, successful updating inserts the concrete literal/type observation while retaining the source marker and empty diagnostic expectation, and a subsequent non-updating run passes without further file changes. This would detect the plausible regression of updating Sage observations before inspecting rustc failure. The second associated test, blessing_gate_is_justified_by_implementation_structure, is explicitly an explanatory no-op: its pass is not behavioral evidence. Its structural rationale is supported by the inspected control flow, as the RFD deliberately specifies; it supplies no claim of exhaustive failure injection. The structural review accounts for every preparation stage and all three output kinds, beyond the executable rustc-mismatch scenario.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test callsite_updates blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates -- --exact: one test passed. Added only the essential rustc::check blessing association with coordinator authorization, ran cargo fmt, restarted the review against the resulting inputs, and ran cargo build successfully (existing warnings). No production behavior was changed; no behavioral bug or missing claim aspect remains. Separate mandatory quality/sanity checks for the marker-only edit were handed to the coordinator after the agent limit prevented spawning a reviewer.

Fresh review after coordinated changes: compared every newly captured initial fragment and association against the previously inspected inputs. The claim, run/prepare boundary, rustc adapter, and both associated test bodies retain their behavior; the callsite test adds only its annotation_validation association. mod.rs adds a compiler-qualification matrix test and an existing-test association, neither changing production flow. observe.rs now appends an explicit unsupported-checking diagnostic for each enum discriminant during whole-crate traversal; these diagnostics flow into the same frozen diagnostic collection and exhaustive matching before any output is returned. Therefore newly detected enum errors remain subject to the same blessing barrier, with no new expectation path. I inspected these changes directly and recaptured parser, policy, and RFD dependencies. The earlier focused test and build executions are historical execution evidence; this refresh is source assessment, not a claim to have rerun tests after the enum change. All current associated entries remain ordinary, with no deferred functionality claimed by this gate review.
